shared_elements: low-relief carving on an upright slab/stela format
human figures (A) and anthropomorphic/zoomorphic glyph heads (B)
registers or rows organizing the content
script-like signs (A has a small column of signs; B is entirely glyphic)
justification: Both are relief-carved upright slabs organized into registers, and both include sign-like elements, some of which in B read as small faces echoing the human profiles in A. But A depicts a narrative figural scene — a large standing profile figure with raised arm facing a seated/attendant figure under a canopy, with offerings and animals below — while B is a pure grid of repeated block-shaped glyphs with no scene, figures at scale, or interaction; the shared traits are generic to relief-carved monuments rather than specific iconographic conventions.
